_standing: 2026-09-20 - the second case the Track 2 pipeline is demonstrated on. Public knowledge only: no allele in any person is asserted here, and nothing in this file comes from the proband's record. Every identifier and every PMID below was resolved live before this file was committed (UniProt REST, HGNC REST, EBI OLS4 for MONDO, NCBI E-utilities for PubMed, and build/reference-scratch/phenotype.hpoa for the OMIM disease name); anything that could not be resolved is null with a note, never a guess. Coordinate-free by rule.
picked_by: a second mosaic-variegated-aneuploidy gene with a different disease, a different tumour and its own public phenotype annotation: TRIP13 causes MVA3 (OMIM 617598, MONDO:0054736) and the reported malignancy is nephroblastoma in 6 of 6 annotated cases, not rhabdomyosarcoma. It shares the spindle assembly checkpoint with the template case, so a transfer that works is a statement about the pipeline rather than about how unlike the two cases are - and it shares no disease query, no clinical term list, no tumour context and no standard-of-care drug with it

mechanism.class: loss-of-function, biallelic (public literature; this card asserts no variant in any person)
mechanism.status: demonstration only: the transfer card exists to run the pipeline on a second case, not to diagnose anyone. The mechanism below is what the cited literature states about TRIP13-related MVA3
mechanism.pathway: spindle assembly checkpoint (SAC) - MAD2 conformational switching and mitotic checkpoint complex (MCC) disassembly by the TRIP13 AAA+ ATPase with p31comet (MAD2L1BP)
mechanism.immediate_effect: loss of TRIP13 ATPase activity leaves MAD2 stuck in its closed, checkpoint-active conformation and the MCC undisassembled; the checkpoint cannot be silenced or reset, and error correction at the kinetochore fails
downstream: mosaic variegated aneuploidy (different chromosomes in different cells)
cancer predisposition, with nephroblastoma (Wilms tumour) the reported malignancy

literature.role: Yost 2017 (Nat Genet): biallelic TRIP13 mutations predispose to Wilms tumor and chromosome missegregation - the MVA3 disease definition and the tumour context
Eytan 2015 (PNAS): mode of interaction of the TRIP13 AAA-ATPase with the Mad2-binding protein p31comet and with mitotic checkpoint complexes - the D3 axis
2017 (Nat Commun): mechanistic insight into TRIP13-catalyzed Mad2 structural transition and spindle checkpoint silencing

repurposing_directions.name: SAC reinforcement / chromosomal-instability reduction
repurposing_directions.rationale: the same direction the template card asks, on this case's checkpoint: agents that prolong mitotic checkpoint arrest or stabilise kinetochore-microtubule attachments. Seeds are the checkpoint core plus TRIP13 and its partner p31comet (MAD2L1BP)

repurposing_directions.name: aneuploidy-selective stress exploitation
repurposing_directions.rationale: aneuploid cells carry proteotoxic and energy stress whatever caused the aneuploidy, so this direction's seed set is the case-agnostic one: AMPK energy stress, the HSP90/HSF1 chaperone axis, autophagy and the proteasome, and the TFEB lysosomal response. Caveat carried over unchanged: this kills aneuploid cells, so it is a tumour-context and chemoprevention angle, not a treatment of the constitutional mosaic state

repurposing_directions.name: TRIP13 / p31comet proteostasis axis
repurposing_directions.rationale: this case's own mechanism direction, and the one that differs most from the template's: TRIP13 is an AAA+ ATPase that, with p31comet (MAD2L1BP), extracts MAD2 from the mitotic checkpoint complex (PMID 26324890, 29208896). A loss-of-function AAA+ ATPase is a protein-remodelling problem, so the seeds are the axis itself plus the drugged arms of cellular proteostasis - the related AAA+ ATPase VCP, the proteasome, and the HSP90/HSP70 chaperones

repurposing_directions.name: cancer surveillance in the nephroblastoma context
repurposing_directions.rationale: the reported malignancy of this case is nephroblastoma, so this is the tumour-context direction and the only one the automated rungs 4 and 5 apply to. Seeds are the genes the Wilms tumour literature drugs or targets: the WT1/IGF2 developmental axis, WNT/beta-catenin, TP53, mTOR and VEGFA
